anomalies.observed: On the EthernetAndPower sheet, the barrel-jack switch contact J7 pin 3 is wired to NET0032, which is also the anode of the battery-isolation diode U11 (U11 pin 2) and the positive terminal of the 18650 holder U2. J7 pin 2 is tied to GND, and the in-sheet note states '2 and 3 are shorted with no plug'. With no DC plug inserted the normally-closed 2–3 contact therefore connects the battery positive (NET0032) directly to GND.
anomalies.expected: The specification requires the switch contact to carry the battery return, not the battery positive: 'J4.3→BAT-' and 'the jack's internal switch keeps the battery's return path connected to GND by default, and inserting a DC plug breaks that short — disconnecting the battery.' Pin 3 should sit on BAT− (the cell negative), so the 2–3 short ties the cell return to GND instead of shorting the cell.

evidence.quote: J7 Barrel_Jack_Switch: '2 and 3 are shorted with no plug / 1 is center, center is positive'; pin 2 → GND, pin 3 → NET0032; U11 SS2040FL pin 2 (anode) → NET0032, pin 1 (cathode) → NET0022 (BAT+)

Netlist: `J4.1→BAT+` (center/positive), `J4.2→GND` (sleeve), `J4.3→BAT-` ... inserting a DC plug breaks that short — disconnecting the battery ... `a1d9676` 'Meshinger 1.0 rev B WARNING THE DC PLUG PINS ARE WRONG, SHORTS BATTERY!'

anomalies.impact: When the board runs on the 18650 with no adapter plugged in, the cell is dead-shortened through the jack's closed 2–3 contact, exactly the 'SHORTS BATTERY' defect the spec says was fixed in rev D. This would blow the cell / diode and prevent USB/adapter power from disconnecting the battery.

parsed.summary: The EPD driver, keyboard, microSD, regulator and signal mapping match the specification (with references simply renumbered in this build), but the DC barrel jack's battery-disconnect switch pin (J7.3) appears tied to the battery-positive / diode-anode net (NET0032) rather than to BAT−, so the normally-closed 2–3 contact shorts the cell to ground when no plug is inserted — reproducing the documented 'SHORTS BATTERY' defect.
